cohort: The study included 105,928 mother-infant dyads of term liveborn infants delivered between 2011 and 2022, whose mothers had no documented thyroid disease or chronic medication administration other than SSRIs.
finding: SSRI treatment during pregnancy was not a significant contributor to newborn total thyroxine (TT4) levels, suggesting no direct effect on the newborn's hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroidal axis adaptation.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was more common among SSRI-treated mothers compared to the general population (p < 0.001).
birth_weight: Infants of SSRI-treated mothers had lower WHO-classified birthweight z-scores (-0.25 +- 0.93 vs -0.04 +- 0.92, p < 0.001) and a higher rate of small-for-gestational-age infants (13.4% vs 8.2%, p < 0.001).
